 This appeal coming on for hearing this day, the court passe  ORDER Heard on IA No.15586/2022,which is an application filed under Section 5 of Limitation Act for condonation of 31 days in filing of the appeal.
Considering the averments mentioned in the application, which is supported by affidavit and in absence of opposition, same is allowed and delay of 31 days in filing of the appeal is hereby condoned.
Accordingly, IA No.15586/2022 stands disposed of.
Also heard on admission.
Admit.
With the consent of learned counsel for the appellants, heard final arguments.

This is an appeal filed by the appellants/claimants under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act,
1988 against the award dated 01/08/2022 passed by 25th Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Jabalpur (M.P.) in MACC No.3828/2019.

By the impugned award, the learned Claims Tribunal awarded a total sum of Rs.9,84,200/- (Nine Lakhs Eighty Four Thousand Two Hundred) with interest @ 6% per annum to the appellants/claimants for the death of Laxman Barman aged about 19 years, who died in motor vehicle accident.
According to claimants i.e. appellants herein, the compensation awarded by the learned Claims Tribunal is on lower side and hence, needs to be enhanced.

2. Since, this Appeal is for the enhancement in the compensation amount awarded by the Claims Tribunal, hence the question that arises for consideration is whether any case for enhancement in compensation awarded by the learned Claims Tribunal on facts and evidence adduced, is made out and if so to what extent?
3.
It is not necessary to narrate the entire facts in detail, such as how the accident occurred, who was negligent in driving the offending vehicle, who is liable for paying compensation etc.
It is for the reason that firstly all these findings are recorded in favour of appellants/claimants by the Tribunal.

Secondly, the findings though recorded in favour of claimants are not under challenge at the instance of any of the respondents such as owner/driver or insurance company either by way of Smt. Kamla Bai Barman vs Mohammad Nisar on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/64327427/
2 filing an appeal or cross-objection.

sentences.text: In this view of the matter, there is no justification to burden this order by detailing facts on all these issues.
4. Learned counsel for the appellants submits that in a motor accident which took place on 19/08/2019, Laxman Berman aged about 19 years died leaving behind his parents.

As the deceased was an unskilled labourer, therefore, learned Tribunal assessed the income of deceased @
Rs.6,000/- (Six Thousand) per month.

For the purpose of computation the amount of loss of dependency and added 40% towards future prospect, due to which monthly income of deceased comes to Rs.8,400/- (Eight Thousand Four Hundred) per month and Rs.1,00,800/- yearly (One Lakh Eight Hundred) and keeping in view that deceased was unmarried, learned Claims Tribunal deducted 1/2 towards personal expenses i.e. Rs.50,400/-(Fifty Thousand Four Hundred).

Keeping in view the age of deceased also applied the multiplier of 18 and awarded a sum of Rs.9,07,200/-
(Nine Lakhs Seven Thousand Two Hundred) towards loss of dependency and awarded Rs.16,500/-
(Sixteen Thousand Five Hundred) towards funeral expenses, Rs.16,500/- (Sixteen Thousand Five Hundred) towards loss of estate and Rs.44,000/- (Forty Four Thousand) towards loss of filial consortium to appellant No.1 /mother of deceased.

Learned Tribunal awarded total sum of Rs.9,84,200/-
(Nine Lakhs Eighty Four Thousand Two Hundred).
5. Learned counsel for the appellants further submitted that though the deceased was an unskilled labourer, but the alleged incident is of the year 2019, so the learned Claims Tribunal committed error in assessing the income of the deceased as Rs.6,000/- (Three Thousand) per month, because as per Minimum Wages Act the income of an unskilled labour in the year 2019 was Rs.7,700/-
(Seven Thousand Seven Hundred) per month.
It is submitted that no amount has been awarded by the learned Claims Tribunal towards filial consortium to father of appellant i.e. appellant No.2.
Accordingly, it is prayed that the appeal be allowed and amount of compensation be enhanced substantially.
6. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent No.3 submits that the amount awarded by the learned Tribunal is just and proper and no case for enhancement is made out.
It is prayed that the appeal be dismissed.
7. I have heard the submissions made by learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

8. The alleged incident is of the year 2019, therefore, income of the deceased assessed by the learned Claims Tribunal as Rs.6,000/- (Six Thousand) per month appears to be on lower side, which ought to have been Rs.7,700/- (Seven Thousand Seven Hundred) per month.
Keeping in view the law laid down by Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma Vs. DTC, 2009 (6) SCC 121 the multiplier of 18 has rightly been applied by the learned Claims Tribunal.

Learned Claims Tribunal has added 40%
towards future prospects, keeping in view the law laid down by Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi & ors (2017) 16 SCC 680.

sentences.text: 1/2 is to be deducted towards personal expenses of the deceased, which comes to Rs.5,390/- (Five Thousand Three Hundred Ninety).

Thus, yearly income will comes to Rs.64,680/- (Sixty Four Thousand Six Hundred Eighty) and thereafter multiplier of 18 will be applied for the purpose of computation of amount towards loss of dependency, which comes to Rs.11,64,240/- (Eleven Lakhs Sixty Four Thousand Two Hundred Forty).

10. It also appears that the Tribunal has not awarded any amount for loss of filial consortium to the father of the deceased i.e. appellant No.2, which should be awarded as Rs.44,000/- in the light of the principle laid down in the case of Janabai wd/o Dinkarrao Ghorpade vs. ICICI Lombord Insurance Company Ltd. (2022) 10 SCC 512 and Magma General Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Nanu Ram @ Chuhru Ram & ors.

In view of above discussion, appellants/claimants shall be entitled for the following amount of compensation :-
 Rs.11,64,240/- Towards loss of dependency  Rs.88,000/- Towards loss of filial consortiu  (Rs.44,000x2)
 Rs.16,500/- Towards loss of estate  Rs.16,500/- Towards funeral expenses ---------------------------------------------------------------------
Rs.12,85,240/- Total ---------------------------------------------------------------------
12.

Thus, the appellants/claimants will be entitled for a total sum of Rs.12,85,240/- (Twelve Lakhs Eight Five Thousands Two Hundred Forty) instead of Rs.9,84,200/- (Nine Lakhs Eight Four Thousands Two Hundred).

Thus, there shall be enhancement to the tune of Rs.3,01,040/- (Three Lakhs One Thousand Forty), which shall fetch interest @ 6% per annum from the date of filing of claim petition till the date of actual payment (except the period of delay).
The payment be made within a period of 60 days from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order.
Other terms and condition of the award shall remain intact.

13. It is pertinent to mention here that the appellants have valued the appeal as Rs.2,60,000/- (Two Lakhs Sixty Thousands) and paid the Court fee as per valuation, therefore, appellants are directed to pay the Court fee on additional amount of Rs.41,040/- (Forty One Thousands Forty) also within a period of 30 days from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order.
If the Court fee is not paid within the stipulated period, then this order will be restricted only up to the amount of Rs.2,60,000/- (Two Lakhs Sixty Thousands).

Enhanced amount shall be paid with interest within Smt. Kamla Bai Barman vs Mohammad Nisar on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/64327427/
4 sixty days from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order.
